title: The Weekend - Cooking A Thanksgiving Dinner
audio: mp3/168. The Weekend - Cooking A Thanksgiving Dinner.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: And my name is Catherine and today we have an advanced media level lesson so that's the very highest of our levels.
segments.zh: 我叫凯瑟琳，今天我们有一节高级媒体水平的课程，这是我们最高级别的课程。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And we're going to be talking about a very popular tradition in North America, a Thanksgiving dinner.
segments.zh: 我们将谈论北美非常流行的传统，即感恩节晚餐。

segments.en: Okay, so Thanksgiving is a very special holiday for Americans and Canadians also celebrate it.
segments.zh: 好的，所以对美国人来说，感恩节是一个非常特别的节日，加拿大人也庆祝它。

segments.en: And different dates, right?
segments.zh: 而且日期还不一样，对吧？

segments.en: Canadians have it on a different date.
segments.zh: 加拿大的日期不一样。

segments.en: In fact, I'm not sure what the Canadian date is but Americans celebrate it at the end of November.
segments.zh: 事实上，我不确定加拿大的日期是什么，但美国人在 11 月底庆祝它。

segments.en: The day changes every year because it's a Thursday.
segments.zh: 这一天每年都在变化，因为它是星期四。

segments.en: But we usually have the day off from work or school and we all eat together and celebrate the year and celebrate the harvest and celebrate our families and friends.
segments.zh: 但我们通常会在工作或学校休息一天，我们一起吃饭，庆祝这一年，庆祝收获，庆祝我们的家人和朋友。

segments.en: So this tradition of Thanksgiving, what do you commemorate or what do you celebrate?
segments.zh: 那么这个感恩节的传统，你纪念什么或庆祝什么？

segments.en: Well, we actually celebrate the first harvest that the pilgrims had when they were right off the boat in New England.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们实际上庆祝朝圣者在新英格兰下船时的第一次收获。

segments.en: So that's the eastern part of America.
segments.zh: 这就是美国的东部。

segments.en: These people had come from England and they were trying to find a new land and a new life and they ended up in the Massachusetts area and they didn't know how to farm.
segments.zh: 这些人来自英格兰，他们试图找到新的土地和新的生活，最终来到马萨诸塞州地区，他们不知道如何耕种。

segments.en: They didn't know how to work the land.
segments.zh: 他们不知道如何耕种这片土地。

segments.en: And so the Native Americans who were living there at the time helped them out, helped them grow corn, helped them find out how to use the land in a productive way.
segments.zh: 因此，当时居住在那里的美洲原住民帮助他们，帮助他们种植玉米，帮助他们了解如何以富有成效的方式使用这片土地。

segments.en: And so when that first harvest happened, everyone was able to grow, it was actually a year after they arrived, everyone was able to grow corn and food and crops and then they all shared a meal together to celebrate this wonderful occasion.
segments.zh: 所以当第一次收获发生时，每个人都能够有收成，实际上是在他们到达一年后，每个人都能够种出玉米、食物和庄稼，然后他们一起分享了一顿饭来庆祝这个美好的时刻。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: And it actually helped them survive the winter because most of the pilgrims, most of the settlers, they died during the first winter.
segments.zh: 它实际上帮助他们度过了冬天，因为大多数朝圣者，大多数定居者，他们在第一个冬天死去。

segments.en: And so this was a really great, great thing for them.
segments.zh: 所以这对他们来说是一件非常棒的事情。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: That's really interesting, an interesting aspect of history and why this is celebrated mostly as you say in North America and Canada and that's why many other countries don't really have it.
segments.zh: 这真的很有趣，是历史的一个有趣方面，也说明了为什么大家如你所说主要在北美和加拿大庆祝它，这就是为什么许多其他国家并没有这个节日。

segments.en: It's a popular get together and what you usually have is a turkey, right?
segments.zh: 这是一个很受欢迎的聚会，你通常吃的是火鸡，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So a turkey is a very big bird and they go gobble, gobble, gobble, gobble.
segments.zh: 所以火鸡是一种很大的鸟，它们会发出咯咯咯的叫声。

segments.en: And they have that kind of really red long kind of thing on their necks and big tail or big tail feathers.
segments.zh: 他们的脖子上有那种红色的长长的东西，大尾巴或大尾羽。

segments.en: And they're delicious.
segments.zh: 而且它们很好吃。

segments.en: But the funny thing is about turkey that there's a chemical in it that makes you very sleepy.
segments.zh: 但有趣的是，火鸡里面有一种化学物质，会让你很困。

segments.en: Well, not a chemical, there's a protein in it that makes you very sleepy.
segments.zh: 好吧，不是化学物质，里面有一种蛋白质，让你很困。

segments.en: Oh really?
segments.zh: 哦，真的吗？

segments.en: I didn't know that.
segments.zh: 我之前不知道这件事。

segments.en: So after you eat dinner on Thanksgiving, everyone falls asleep on the sofa.
segments.zh: 所以在你在感恩节吃完晚饭后，每个人都在沙发上睡着了。

segments.en: Well, Thanksgiving meals in the United States are very, very big.
segments.zh: 嗯，美国的感恩节大餐非常非常大。

segments.en: They're very elaborate, right?
segments.zh: 它们非常精致，对吧？

segments.en: You'll not only have turkey, but you have pumpkin pie and you have mashed potatoes and gravy and just like a table full of food.
segments.zh: 你不仅有火鸡，而且你有南瓜派，还有土豆泥和肉汁，就像一张满是食物的桌子。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And it's a way to celebrate, well to give thanks for all the things that you have.
segments.zh: 这是一种庆祝的方式，感谢你拥有的所有东西。

segments.en: And so we like to cook a lot of food to celebrate that.
segments.zh: 所以我们喜欢做很多食物来庆祝这一点。

segments.en: And they're all fall foods.
segments.zh: 它们都是秋季食品。

segments.en: So squash, pumpkin, potatoes, things like that.
segments.zh: 所以有南瓜类蔬菜、南瓜、土豆等等。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we have a dialogue here.
segments.zh: 所以我们在这里进行对话。

segments.en: So it's just that.
segments.zh: 所以就是这样。

segments.en: It's a guy who is preparing a turkey dinner and also preparing pumpkin pie.
segments.zh: 这是一个正在准备火鸡晚餐并准备南瓜派的人。

segments.en: But he's doing it in a very peculiar way.
segments.zh: 但他正在以一种非常奇特的方式做到这一点。

segments.en: So why don't we listen to the dialogue and then we'll come back and just talk a little bit about the different terms that he used.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不听对话，然后我们会回来，谈谈他使用的不同术语。

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to our show.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到我们的节目。

segments.en: Today we are going to learn how to cook the perfect Thanksgiving turkey.
segments.zh: 今天我们将学习如何烹制完美的感恩节火鸡。

segments.en: I will share a secret that I have kept for over 30 years on how to cook the perfect, most mouthwatering, juiciest turkey in the world.
segments.zh: 我将分享一个我保守了 30 多年的秘密，关于如何烹饪世界上最完美、最令人垂涎、最多汁的火鸡。

segments.en: Let's get started.
segments.zh: 我们开始吧。

segments.en: First of all, we must bring out our key ingredient, whiskey.
segments.zh: 首先，拿出我们的关键配料：威士忌。

segments.en: You see, the grains used to make whiskey along with the alcohol brings out the flavor of the turkey meat.
segments.zh: 你看，用来制作威士忌的谷物和酒精一起带出了火鸡肉的味道。

segments.en: Let's pour one cup of whiskey on the turkey and serve yourself a cup as well.
segments.zh: 让我们把一杯威士忌倒在火鸡上，也给自己倒一杯。

segments.en: Cheers!
segments.zh: 干杯！

segments.en: Ah, that's good 12 year whiskey right there.
segments.zh: 啊，那是很好的 12 年威士忌。

segments.en: Okay, back to our turkey.
segments.zh: 好了，继续做我们的火鸡。

segments.en: Preheat your oven to 475 degrees Fahrenheit.
segments.zh: 将烤箱预热至 475 华氏度。

segments.en: Now have another cup of whiskey.
segments.zh: 现在再来一杯威士忌。

segments.en: Now that the oven is hot, we place our bird on a rack inside a roasting pan.
segments.zh: 烤箱热了以后，把火鸡放到烤盘里的烤架上。

segments.en: Let's add some whiskey to give it some extra flavor.
segments.zh: 让我们添加一些威士忌，给它一些额外的味道。

segments.en: And let's have another cup.
segments.zh: 让我们再来一杯。

segments.en: That hit the spot.
segments.zh: 真过瘾。

segments.en: There we go.
segments.zh: 好了。

segments.en: We can leave it in there for the next 45 minutes.
segments.zh: 我们可以在接下来的 45 分钟内将它留在那里。

segments.en: In the meantime, let's have another sip of whiskey and start with our delicious pumpkin pie.
segments.zh: 与此同时，让我们再喝一口威士忌，从我们美味的南瓜派开始。

segments.en: Lightly whisk together two eggs and the extra yolk in a large bowl.
segments.zh: 把两个鸡蛋和额外的一个蛋黄放进大碗里，轻轻打匀。

segments.en: Once that's ready, we can put sugar, spices such as cloves, grated nutmeg, and cinnamon with some cream and dark rum into a saucepan.
segments.zh: 准备好后，我们可以将糖，以及丁香、磨碎的肉豆蔻和肉桂等香料，连同一些奶油和黑朗姆酒放入炖锅中。

segments.en: Gently bring up to simmering point, stirring occasionally.
segments.zh: 用小火加热至微微沸腾，偶尔搅拌。

segments.en: Now you may notice that we are using some dark rum in this pie.
segments.zh: 现在您可能会注意到我们在这个馅饼中使用了一些黑朗姆酒。

segments.en: This is because the richness of the pumpkin is beautifully enhanced by the dark rum.
segments.zh: 因为黑朗姆酒能很好地提升南瓜的浓郁风味。

segments.en: So to celebrate this great occasion, pour yourself a glass.
segments.zh: 所以为了庆祝这个伟大的时刻，给自己倒一杯。

segments.en: Cheers!
segments.zh: 干杯！

segments.en: Now that we have finished with the filling, let's bake the pie for 45 to 50 minutes until the filling has puffed up around the edges and the center is almost set.
segments.zh: 现在我们已经完成了馅料，让我们烤馅饼 45 到 50 分钟，直到馅料在边缘膨胀起来，中心几乎凝固。

segments.en: All done!
segments.zh: 全部完成！

segments.en: A cup of rum to celebrate the completion of this great Thanksgiving dinner.
segments.zh: 一杯朗姆酒庆祝这场盛大的感恩节晚餐的完成。

segments.en: After waiting for an hour and having a couple of drinks, it's time to check on our turkey.
segments.zh: 等了一个小时，喝了几杯，是时候检查我们的火鸡了。

segments.en: Take the turkey out of the oven.
segments.zh: 把火鸡从烤箱里拿出来。

segments.en: Pick the turkey off of the ground.
segments.zh: 把火鸡从地上捡起来。

segments.en: Don't worry, it will add flavor to this recipe.
segments.zh: 别担心，它会为这个食谱增添风味。

segments.en: Now also remove the pie from the oven and serve while still hot.
segments.zh: 现在也从烤箱中取出馅饼，趁热食用。

segments.en: Cheers and Happy Thanksgiving!
segments.zh: 干杯和感恩节快乐！

segments.en: All right we're back so I think this is going to be one great Thanksgiving dinner for him.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们回来了，所以我认为这对他来说将是一顿很棒的感恩节晚餐。

segments.en: Oh my gosh and talking about this is making me so hungry.
segments.zh: 哦，我的天哪，谈论这个让我如此饥饿。

segments.en: This always happens when we have food lessons.
segments.zh: 当我们有食物课程时，这总是发生。

segments.en: What about do you have any family members who actually drink a little bit too much during Thanksgiving?
segments.zh: 你们有没有在感恩节期间喝得太多的家人呢？

segments.en: Yes and I won't say who.
segments.zh: 是的，我不会说是谁。

segments.en: So as he was preparing the Thanksgiving dinner, he mentioned a couple of things.
segments.zh: 所以在他准备感恩节晚餐的时候，他提到了一些事情。

segments.en: For example, a mouth-watering turkey.
segments.zh: 例如，令人垂涎的火鸡。

segments.en: Mouth-watering so this is a way to say appetizing.
segments.zh: 令人垂涎的，所以这是一种说开胃的方式。

segments.en: You know when you see something delicious on TV and your mouth starts to water, you're salivating.
segments.zh: 你知道，当你在电视上看到美味的东西、嘴开始流口水时，那就是在流涎。

segments.en: It's like your brain is telling you that you want to eat it.
segments.zh: 就像你的大脑在告诉你你想吃它。

segments.en: And so your mouth starts to water.
segments.zh: 所以你的嘴开始流口水。

segments.en: So we say that something that's very appetizing, something that looks like it will taste very very good, it's mouth-watering.
segments.zh: 所以我们说，非常开胃、看起来会非常非常好吃的东西，就是 mouth-watering（令人垂涎的）。

segments.en: All right so he was preparing a mouth-watering turkey.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以他正在准备一只令人垂涎的火鸡。

segments.en: So moving on, he mentioned that he had a key ingredient for his turkey and it was whiskey.
segments.zh: 所以接下来，他提到他的火鸡有一个关键配料，那就是威士忌。

segments.en: Not only whiskey but 12-year whiskey.
segments.zh: 不仅是威士忌，还有 12 年的威士忌。

segments.en: Okay so the thing about whiskey is that oftentimes on the label of a bottle they'll advertise how old the whiskey is because you pay more for older whiskeys.
segments.zh: 好吧，威士忌的特点是，通常在瓶子的标签上会标明威士忌的年份，因为年份越久的威士忌越贵。

segments.en: They just have better taste in many cases.
segments.zh: 很多情况下，它们的味道就是更好。

segments.en: In this case it's a 12-year whiskey.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，它是 12 年的威士忌。

segments.en: That means that it was stored in a cask for 12 years to let it age and then they sell it after 12 years and so that's the special ingredient.
segments.zh: 这意味着它在木桶里存放了 12 年进行陈酿，然后 12 年后才出售，所以这就是那个特殊的配料。

segments.en: That's the special ingredient, 12-year whiskey.
segments.zh: 这就是特殊成分，12 年威士忌。

segments.en: And well he not only put it on the turkey but also he had a couple of drinks himself and in one of those he mentioned that hit the spot.
segments.zh: 好吧，他不仅把它倒在火鸡上，自己也喝了几杯，而且谈到其中一杯时他说 that hit the spot。

segments.en: That hit the spot.
segments.zh: 真过瘾。

segments.en: What spot?
segments.zh: 什么地方？

segments.en: The spot.
segments.zh: 就是那个 spot。

segments.en: Okay so this is a really common phrase in English that we use to say that something is very satisfying.
segments.zh: 好吧，这是英语中一个非常常见的短语，我们常常说某事非常令人满意。

segments.en: So that hit the spot.
segments.zh: 所以 that hit the spot 就是这个意思。

segments.en: And not only for drinks right?
segments.zh: 而且不只是为了喝酒吗？

segments.en: No you could use it for food or anything really.
segments.zh: 不，你可以用它作为食物或任何东西。

segments.en: So in this case I could say, oh so hungry that sandwich really hit the spot.
segments.zh: 所以这里我可以说，哦，我太饿了，那个三明治真是恰到好处。

segments.en: I really needed to eat right now and that sandwich was perfect.
segments.zh: 我现在真的需要吃饭，那个三明治很完美。

segments.en: That was perfect.
segments.zh: 那是完美的。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that hit the spot.
segments.zh: 所以 that hit the spot 就是这个意思。

segments.en: Now when he referred to the turkey, in one occasion he said we place our bird on a rack.
segments.zh: 现在，当他提到火鸡时，有一次他说我们把我们的鸟放在架子上。

segments.en: Alright so what's a bird and what's the rack?
segments.zh: 好吧，什么是鸟，什么是架子？

segments.en: Okay so this is really interesting.
segments.zh: 好吧，这真的很有趣。

segments.en: We talk about the turkey often times when we're making commercials or talking about recipes as the bird.
segments.zh: 在做广告或谈论食谱时，我们常常把火鸡叫作 the bird。

segments.en: So you want to take out the bird, you want to open the packaging.
segments.zh: 所以你想取出鸟，你想打开包装。

segments.en: So the bird is the turkey.
segments.zh: 所以这只鸟就是火鸡。

segments.en: A turkey is a kind of bird.
segments.zh: 火鸡是一种鸟。

segments.en: You can say this about chicken as well because it's another kind of bird.
segments.zh: 你也可以这样说鸡肉，因为它是另一种鸟。

segments.en: But this is kind of a colloquial term in cooking for whatever bird you're cooking.
segments.zh: 但这是烹饪时的一个口语说法，用来指你正在烹饪的任何禽类。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And when you're placing it on a rack, what's a rack?
segments.zh: 当你把它放在架子上时，什么是架子？

segments.en: Okay so in our ovens, an oven is a kitchen appliance that you have that heats up food.
segments.zh: 好吧，在我们的烤箱中，烤箱是一种厨房用具，可以加热食物。

segments.en: But it's not like a microwave, it's much stronger.
segments.zh: 但它不像微波炉，它更强大。

segments.en: And so inside there are metal bars.
segments.zh: 所以里面有金属条。

segments.en: We don't have, they're like shelves but they're open.
segments.zh: 它们像架子，但是是镂空敞开的。

segments.en: And so these metal bars are called a rack.
segments.zh: 所以这些金属条就叫 rack（烤架）。

segments.en: So you put the turkey in the oven on the rack.
segments.zh: 所以你把火鸡放在架子上的烤箱里。

segments.en: Right, you can't put it on the base of the oven because then it would burn up.
segments.zh: 是的，你不能把它放在烤箱的底部，因为它会烧掉。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And you don't have a shelf because that would be a problem.
segments.zh: 而且你没有架子，因为那会是个问题。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And well, moving on the instructions when he was preparing the pumpkin pie, he told us to lightly whisk together two eggs.
segments.zh: 好吧，在他准备南瓜派的时候，他告诉我们轻轻地把两个鸡蛋搅拌在一起。

segments.en: So we have a verb here, to whisk.
segments.zh: 所以我们在这里有一个动词，搅拌。

segments.en: To whisk.
segments.zh: 搅拌。

segments.en: So that's not only a verb but a noun as well, right?
segments.zh: 所以这不仅仅是一个动词，也是一个名词，对吧？

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: It's an instrument.
segments.zh: 它是一种器具。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And this is a verb we often use with eggs.
segments.zh: 这是我们经常与鸡蛋一起使用的动词。

segments.en: So to whisk eggs.
segments.zh: 所以要打鸡蛋。

segments.en: You can also whisk like sauce for a salad, so like a salad dressing.
segments.zh: 你也可以像沙拉一样搅拌酱汁，就像沙拉酱一样。

segments.en: But it's a way that we stir something.
segments.zh: 但这是我们搅动一些东西的一种方式。

segments.en: And so oftentimes we have an instrument called a whisk that's not like a fork.
segments.zh: 很多时候，我们有一种叫 whisk（打蛋器）的器具，它不像叉子。

segments.en: It actually looks kind of funny.
segments.zh: 它实际上看起来有点有趣。

segments.en: It's got bars on it.
segments.zh: 它上面有金属条。

segments.en: Like wire that kind of make a circle.
segments.zh: 就像金属丝围成一个圆圈那样。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And they are very thin wires.
segments.zh: 它们是非常细的金属丝。

segments.en: And you usually stir very, very, very quickly.
segments.zh: 你通常会非常、非常、非常快地搅拌。

segments.en: Especially if you have eggs, this will break up the egg and it becomes kind of like foamy.
segments.zh: 特别是打鸡蛋时，这会把鸡蛋打散，变得有点像泡沫。

segments.en: Foamy, yeah.
segments.zh: 泡沫，是的。

segments.en: To make like an omelet for example.
segments.zh: 例如做一个煎蛋。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So to whisk is a kind of, it's a way to stir.
segments.zh: 所以打发是一种，它是一种搅拌的方式。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And then he mentioned some ingredients such as sugar, spices, and grated nutmeg.
segments.zh: 然后他提到了一些成分，如糖、香料和磨碎的肉豆蔻。

segments.en: So what is this verb, grated nutmeg?
segments.zh: 那么这个动词是什么，磨碎的肉豆蔻呢？

segments.en: Or an adjective, grated.
segments.zh: 或者是个形容词，磨碎的。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So this adjective, grated, means that, well it's a kind of way to cut up something.
segments.zh: 所以 grated 这个形容词的意思是，这是一种把东西弄碎的方式。

segments.en: And so you often hear the term grated cheese.
segments.zh: 所以你经常听到磨碎的奶酪这个词。

segments.en: That means not a big chunk of cheese, but we push it against a board to get little pieces of it to fall off.
segments.zh: 这意味着没有一大块奶酪，但我们将它推到板上，让它的小块脱落。

segments.en: And that's called grated cheese.
segments.zh: 这就是所谓的磨碎奶酪。

segments.en: And so in this case we have grated nutmeg.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，我们有磨碎的肉豆蔻。

segments.en: That means that it's been kind of, the nutmeg comes in, in very small pieces.
segments.zh: 这意味着它有点，肉豆蔻进来，分成很小的部分。

segments.en: Yeah, pieces.
segments.zh: 是的，碎片。

segments.en: And we're breaking it down.
segments.zh: 我们正在分解它。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And he also mentioned something about bringing the sauce to a simmering point.
segments.zh: 他还提到要把酱汁加热到微沸状态。

segments.en: What is that simmering point?
segments.zh: 那个微沸点是什么？

segments.en: Okay, simmering point is a time when you're cooking where the liquid goes from being calm to being very agitated and moving.
segments.zh: 好吧，微沸点是你做饭时，液体从平静变得开始翻动的那一刻。

segments.en: But it's not boiling, right?
segments.zh: 但它不是沸腾的，对吧？

segments.en: No, boiling means you have big bubbles.
segments.zh: 不，沸腾意味着你有大气泡。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Like boiling water.
segments.zh: 像沸水一样。

segments.en: But simmering is where it's kind of little bubbles, there's a little bit of action on the surface of the liquid, but it's not boiling.
segments.zh: 但微沸是有小气泡，液体表面有一点动静，但并没有沸腾。

segments.en: It's in the middle between flat and calm and agitated and boiling.
segments.zh: 它介于平坦、平静、激动和沸腾之间。

segments.en: Okay, so that's the simmering point.
segments.zh: 好吧，这就是微沸点。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And that's pretty much all of the interesting phrases in the dialogue.
segments.zh: 这几乎就是对话中所有有趣的短语。

segments.en: There are a lot more, but we don't really have time to cover that huge amount of rich vocabulary.
segments.zh: 还有很多，但我们真的没时间讲完这么多丰富的词汇。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to this dialogue one last time?
segments.zh: 我们最后再听一遍这段对话吧？

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to our show.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到我们的节目。

segments.en: Today we are going to learn how to cook the perfect Thanksgiving turkey.
segments.zh: 今天我们将学习如何烹制完美的感恩节火鸡。

segments.en: I will share a secret that I have kept for over 30 years on how to cook the perfect, most mouthwatering, juiciest turkey in the world.
segments.zh: 我将分享一个我保守了 30 多年的秘密，关于如何烹饪世界上最完美、最令人垂涎、最多汁的火鸡。

segments.en: Let's get started.
segments.zh: 我们开始吧。

segments.en: First of all, we must bring out our key ingredient, whiskey.
segments.zh: 首先，拿出我们的关键配料：威士忌。

segments.en: You see, the grains used to make whiskey along with the alcohol brings out the flavor of the turkey meat.
segments.zh: 你看，用来制作威士忌的谷物和酒精一起带出了火鸡肉的味道。

segments.en: Let's pour one cup of whiskey on the turkey and serve yourself a cup as well.
segments.zh: 让我们把一杯威士忌倒在火鸡上，也给自己倒一杯。

segments.en: Cheers!
segments.zh: 干杯！

segments.en: Ah, that's good 12-year whiskey right there.
segments.zh: 啊，那是很好的 12 年威士忌。

segments.en: Okay, back to our turkey.
segments.zh: 好的，回到我们的火鸡。

segments.en: Preheat your oven to 475 degrees Fahrenheit.
segments.zh: 将烤箱预热至 475 华氏度。

segments.en: Now have another cup of whiskey.
segments.zh: 现在再来一杯威士忌。

segments.en: Now that the oven is hot, we place our bird on a rack inside a roasting pan.
segments.zh: 烤箱热了以后，把火鸡放到烤盘里的烤架上。

segments.en: Let's add some whiskey to give it some extra flavor.
segments.zh: 让我们添加一些威士忌，给它一些额外的味道。

segments.en: And let's have another cup.
segments.zh: 让我们再来一杯。

segments.en: That hit the spot.
segments.zh: 真过瘾。

segments.en: There we go.
segments.zh: 好了。

segments.en: We can leave it in there for the next 45 minutes.
segments.zh: 我们可以在接下来的 45 分钟内将它留在那里。

segments.en: In the meantime, let's have another sip of whiskey and start with our delicious pumpkin pie.
segments.zh: 与此同时，让我们再喝一口威士忌，从我们美味的南瓜派开始。

segments.en: Lightly whisk together two eggs and the extra yolk in a large bowl.
segments.zh: 把两个鸡蛋和额外的一个蛋黄放进大碗里，轻轻打匀。

segments.en: Once that's ready, we can put sugar, spices such as cloves, grated nutmeg, and cinnamon with some cream and dark rum into a saucepan.
segments.zh: 准备好后，我们可以将糖，以及丁香、磨碎的肉豆蔻和肉桂等香料，连同一些奶油和黑朗姆酒放入炖锅中。

segments.en: Gently bring up to simmering point, stirring occasionally.
segments.zh: 用小火加热至微微沸腾，偶尔搅拌。

segments.en: Now you may notice that we are using some dark rum in this pie.
segments.zh: 现在您可能会注意到我们在这个馅饼中使用了一些黑朗姆酒。

segments.en: This is because the richness of the pumpkin is beautifully enhanced by the dark rum.
segments.zh: 因为黑朗姆酒能很好地提升南瓜的浓郁风味。

segments.en: So to celebrate this great occasion, pour yourself a glass.
segments.zh: 所以为了庆祝这个伟大的时刻，给自己倒一杯。

segments.en: Cheers!
segments.zh: 干杯！

segments.en: Now that we have finished with the filling, let's bake the pie for 45 to 50 minutes until the filling has puffed up around the edges and the center is almost set.
segments.zh: 现在我们已经完成了馅料，让我们烤馅饼 45 到 50 分钟，直到馅料在边缘膨胀起来，中心几乎凝固。

segments.en: All done!
segments.zh: 全部完成！

segments.en: A cup of rum to celebrate the completion of this great Thanksgiving dinner.
segments.zh: 一杯朗姆酒庆祝这场盛大的感恩节晚餐的完成。

segments.en: After waiting for an hour and having a couple of drinks, it's time to check on our turkey.
segments.zh: 等了一个小时，喝了几杯，是时候检查我们的火鸡了。

segments.en: Take the turkey out of the oven.
segments.zh: 把火鸡从烤箱里拿出来。

segments.en: Pick the turkey off of the ground.
segments.zh: 把火鸡从地上捡起来。

segments.en: Don't worry, it will add flavor to this recipe.
segments.zh: 别担心，它会为这个食谱增添风味。

segments.en: Now also remove the pie from the oven and serve while still hot.
segments.zh: 现在也从烤箱中取出馅饼，趁热食用。

segments.en: Cheers and Happy Thanksgiving!
segments.zh: 干杯和感恩节快乐！

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So Thanksgiving dinner, really popular.
segments.zh: 所以感恩节晚餐，真的很受欢迎。

segments.en: Catherine, have you ever cooked or are you into the whole Thanksgiving feast?
segments.zh: 凯瑟琳，你做过饭吗，或者说你喜欢整个感恩节大餐这套吗？

segments.en: I'm very into it.
segments.zh: 我很喜欢。

segments.en: It's my favorite holiday in America, mostly because everyone gets to celebrate it.
segments.zh: 这是我在美国最喜欢的节日，主要是因为每个人都可以庆祝它。

segments.en: It's not religious, so you don't have to worry about other people not celebrating it or not knowing what to do.
segments.zh: 它不是宗教的，所以你不必担心其他人不庆祝或不知道该怎么做。

segments.en: And it's also a celebration about family and food.
segments.zh: 这也是关于家庭和食物的庆祝活动。

segments.en: And so it's just a wonderful experience to have Thanksgiving because you're with everybody.
segments.zh: 因此，感恩节是一次美妙的经历，因为你和每个人在一起。

segments.en: And we always say in America that if someone doesn't have a place to go on Thanksgiving, you should invite them to your house.
segments.zh: 我们在美国总是说，如果有人感恩节没地方去，你就应该邀请他们到你家。

segments.en: And so it's a very inviting and warm holiday.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个非常诱人和温暖的假期。

segments.en: And I love cooking and I love being in the kitchen and I love having people in the house cooking and so yeah, I've definitely been a part of the cooking side of things.
segments.zh: 我喜欢做饭，喜欢待在厨房里，喜欢有人在家里一起做饭，所以没错，我绝对算是负责做饭的那一方。

segments.en: Now in many movies, they kind of mock this holiday because it's a time where everyone gets together, as you say, no matter religion, creed or race.
segments.zh: 现在在很多电影里，他们会有点调侃这个节日，因为这是大家聚在一起的时候，正如你所说，不论宗教、信仰还是种族。

segments.en: And that also causes for a lot of family members to get together and argue and have discussions about politics or talk about family problems and stuff like that.
segments.zh: 这也导致许多家庭成员聚在一起争论和讨论政治或谈论家庭问题之类的东西。

segments.en: So what do you think of that?
segments.zh: 那你怎么看？

segments.en: Well, I think it's an exaggeration, but it happens.
segments.zh: 好吧，我认为这是夸大其词，但它发生了。

segments.en: People get very stressed out during the holidays.
segments.zh: 人们在假期里压力很大。

segments.en: They call it the holidays because this is beginning where you have Thanksgiving and then later Christmas.
segments.zh: 他们称之为「假期季」，因为这是一连串假期的开端，先过感恩节，之后还有圣诞节。

segments.en: But I personally don't have experience with that really on Thanksgiving because it's such a happy holiday for us.
segments.zh: 但我个人在感恩节还真没经历过这种事，因为对我们来说这是一个非常快乐的节日。

segments.en: So and in my family, arguments about politics and history and all that is very encouraged.
segments.zh: 而且在我的家庭里，关于政治、历史的争论以及所有这些，都是很受鼓励的。

segments.en: And so it's just a part of the holiday where we have, we have, you know, one person at the table who says this and the other person says this and you're all drinking and it's just, it's fun.
segments.zh: 所以这只是假期的一部分，我们有，你知道，桌上的一个人说这个，另一个人说这个，而你们都在喝酒，这很有趣。

segments.en: I look forward to it.
segments.zh: 我很期待。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So if you guys have any other questions or doubts about this holiday, because as we say, it's very common in North America and Canada, you can come to our website, EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 因此，如果你们对这个假期有任何其他问题或疑问，因为正如我们所说，这在北美和加拿大很常见，您可以访问我们的网站 englishpod.com。

segments.en: And if you have any other questions or suggestions, you can leave those there as well.
segments.zh: 如果您有任何其他问题或建议，您也可以将其留在那里。

segments.en: We look forward to hearing what you have to say and happy Thanksgiving.
segments.zh: 我们期待听到您要说的话和感恩节快乐。

segments.en: Happy Thanksgiving.
segments.zh: 感恩节快乐。

segments.en: Bye everyone.
segments.zh: 大家再见。

segments.en: Happy Thanksgiving.
segments.zh: 感恩节快乐。
